contract_plain_english: A symmetric Bernoulli, or Rademacher, random variable takes the values -1 and 1 with probability one half each. A usual Bernoulli(1/2) random variable X is equivalent under the affine recoding Z=2X-1 to a symmetric Bernoulli variable Z (PDF page 4/printed page 15, Definition 2.2.1 and the immediately following paragraph).

source_evidence.observation: The section introduces symmetric Bernoulli random variables as the summands for a concentration inequality concerning sums of i.i.d. variables.
A random variable has symmetric Bernoulli distribution, also called Rademacher distribution, when it takes the values -1 and 1 with probability 1/2 each.
A random variable X has the usual Bernoulli distribution with parameter 1/2 if and only if the affine transform Z=2X-1 has symmetric Bernoulli distribution.

binders: X is a scalar-valued random variable on an implicit probability space (PDF page 4/printed page 15, Definition 2.2.1, phrase 'A random variable X').
In the affine-equivalence paragraph, Z is the random variable defined from X by Z=2X-1 (PDF page 4/printed page 15, paragraph immediately following Definition 2.2.1).
conclusions: X has symmetric Bernoulli distribution if and only if it takes the two values -1 and 1 with probabilities P{X=-1}=1/2 and P{X=1}=1/2 (PDF page 4/printed page 15, Definition 2.2.1 and its display).
The name Rademacher distribution is synonymous with symmetric Bernoulli distribution (PDF page 4/printed page 15, Definition 2.2.1, parenthetical 'also called Rademacher distribution').
X has the usual Bernoulli distribution with parameter 1/2 if and only if Z=2X-1 has symmetric Bernoulli distribution (PDF page 4/printed page 15, paragraph immediately following Definition 2.2.1).
definitions_and_conventions: A symmetric Bernoulli variable has support on the two values -1 and 1, each carrying probability 1/2 (PDF page 4/printed page 15, Definition 2.2.1, phrase 'takes values -1 and 1 with probabilities 1/2 each').
The displayed definition states the two exact atom probabilities P{X=-1}=P{X=1}=1/2 (PDF page 4/printed page 15, Definition 2.2.1 display).
Symmetric Bernoulli distribution and Rademacher distribution are two names for the same law (PDF page 4/printed page 15, Definition 2.2.1 parenthetical).
The affine conversion from the usual Bernoulli(1/2) convention to the symmetric convention is exactly x↦2x-1 (PDF page 4/printed page 15, paragraph immediately following Definition 2.2.1).
The affine statement is bidirectional, not merely the forward construction of a symmetric variable from a Bernoulli variable (PDF page 4/printed page 15, phrase 'if and only if').
hypotheses: For the defining characterization, X takes values in a scalar setting containing -1 and 1 and admitting event probabilities (PDF page 4/printed page 15, Definition 2.2.1 and its displayed probability equalities).
For the affine equivalence, X is a random variable for which the transformation 2X-1 is defined (PDF page 4/printed page 15, paragraph immediately following Definition 2.2.1).
implicit_context: The section intends symmetric Bernoulli variables for later concentration inequalities involving sums of i.i.d. variables, but independence and identical distribution are not part of Definition 2.2.1 itself (PDF page 4/printed page 15, Section 2.2 introductory sentence followed by Definition 2.2.1).

The ordinary Bernoulli distribution with parameter 1/2 is invoked as an existing convention rather than separately defined on this page (PDF page 4/printed page 15, paragraph immediately following Definition 2.2.1, phrase 'the (usual) Bernoulli distribution').

Theorem 2.2.2 and its tail inequality begin only after the definition and affine-equivalence paragraph and are not conclusions of this task (PDF page 4/printed page 15, structural boundary at 'Theorem 2.2.2').
